attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stating his personal expectation.

semantics.note: 'I would expect' is an unqualified expectation, so this is a scored forecast that OpenAI will reach Google/Meta scale. The drafter's modality tag 'likely' understates it but does not change the kind. No horizon was given.

contract.note: The contract uses a plain reading of overall business scale and does not let one proxy decide the result. It contradicts the claim only on permanent cessation. This is fair to an open-ended forecast with no named measure. Its 'could become' wording is a bit soft, but the support condition requires actual attainment.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure (2026-03-31) of an $852B private valuation and $2B monthly revenue. A single proxy from the company itself does not establish Google/Meta-comparable scale.
OpenAI's own disclosure (2026-09-08) of over 1B weekly users. Audience reach alone does not settle the business-scale comparison.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The packet holds only OpenAI's own disclosures of valuation, revenue run rate and users. None of them unambiguously shows comparable overall scale to Google or Meta, and OpenAI has not ceased operating. Under the early-resolution rule no conclusive event has occurred, so the claim stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his post. He cites the data but makes the assertion himself.

semantics.note: Faithful restatement of both parts: AI as a reliable road to capital, and more than a quarter of 2023 startup dollars going to AI. It is a historical observation for 2023 year-to-date.

contract.note: The US scope comes from the source the post links to, which is a fair, ordinary reading. 'Reliable' is read as relative funding resilience, which is reasonable. The result depends on the geography choice, since the global share was lower.

evidence.note: Crunchbase, 2023-08-29: more than 1 in 4 US startup dollars went to AI that year, and AI funding was resilient and rising while overall funding fell. This matches both parts of the claim.
Global first-half share was 18%. Different geography and time window, so it limits generalisation rather than contradicting the US claim.
Global AI deal counts fell in Q3 2023. Deal count is a different metric from dollar share; it qualifies but does not refute aggregate resilience.

reviews.rationale: The dataset provider's own analysis, which the post links to, puts AI above 25% of 2023 US startup dollars and describes AI funding as resilient during a broad downturn. The lower global share and falling deal counts are different scopes or metrics and do not contradict the claim as scoped.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence. He reports a third-party cost estimate and adds his own judgment of unsustainability.

semantics.note: Verbatim, with 'estimated' kept. A compound claim: an estimate exists, plus an evaluative judgment that the push to grow is deeply unsustainable.

contract.note: Reading 'unsustainable' as unable to cover its costs without outside financing is a fair, ordinary reading. Picking July–September 2023 is the evaluator's choice. That is strict for 'is estimated', which only refers to an existing estimate, but it does not change the result here.

evidence.note: April 2023 report of an analyst estimate of up to $700k/day, which matches the cost wording. It falls outside the contract period and says nothing about sustainability.
August 2023 report of $80M+ monthly revenue for all of OpenAI. With no matched expense or financing records, it neither proves nor disproves sustainability.

reviews.rationale: An estimate in the stated range did exist, though it predates the contract period. The packet has no matched expense, cash or financing records for the sustainability clause, and revenue alone settles neither side. Because the compound claim needs both clauses, the evidence does not settle it.
